posts.author: Kibu_Cat
posts.body:
Hello!
I am INCREDIBLY new to
RPG Maker
. As in, just installed it last night. I've been messing around with it all day and learning how the engine works, and for the most part, it's incredibly simplistic and has been a dream. However, one thing, despite the endless tutorials online explaining them, alludes me;
Plugins
.
It always seems so simple whenever I see tutorials explaining it, and I understand the process of moving the
.js files
into the
game file
of the project you're working on, however I'm having trouble getting... well, the .js files! Whenever I download something off of
Itch.io
(my current site of choice), it installs as a normal
zip folder
, and if I extract it, there's no javascript files/file to be found! Perhaps I'm being stupid, or missing something?
If someone could explain to me what I'm doing wrong, it would be greatly appreciated. Or if there's some way to specify the kind of file I want things to be downloaded as? I'm not especially tech savvy, so I remain perplexed! Any help at all would literally make my life so much easier, thank you! At least the first hurdle came from something outside the base game!
I have attached below the example plugins I have attempted to install, just in case anyone else actively uses them, and can explain it to me better that way.
Ignore the red circling/crappy attempt at writing, I don't know why I tried to caption it, it's pretty damn obvious where they are
;-;

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body: The file folder it opens is what you go to next. And you may need to go deeper in after that.

what youve shown arent plugins. they both appear to be asset packs. plugins are .js files and if there are none then youre not dealing with plugins. did the itch.io pages for them say they were or contained plugins?
Kibu_Cat said:
I am INCREDIBLY new to
RPG Maker
. As in, just installed it last night.
Click to expand...
i would suggest against playing around with plugins when youre that new. the whole point of them are to change how the base engine works. if youre already unfamiliar with how that works, then youll end up making things more complicated for yourself starting off than necessary.
